transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-10
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Mira - Head of Data), Tom Herrera (Mira - Platform Eng), Priya Raman (Mira - CTO)

Summary:
Brief console walkthrough focusing on per-route usage analytics, cost breakdown by model/route, and how Optimize recommendations (batching, caching, quant profiles) translate to unit economics. Discussed hosted vs dedicated and VPC/privacy requirements for healthcare data. Agreed to pricing follow-up and technical benchmark.

Topics:
- Per-route dashboards and filters (by model, route, environment)
- Token-level and embedding cost breakdowns
- Caching/KV prefix reuse and effect on cost
- Routing policies: region/dedicated/hosted fallbacks
- Compliance: SOC2, VPC, KMS/HSM options

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time today. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, I'm the AE on the account, and Samir's our solutions engineer who will do a lot of the console tour.
[00:12] Aisha (Mira): Hi Jordan, thanks. I have Tom and Priya on our side. We're mainly interested in understanding how you show usage and where cost is coming from per route.
[00:22] Samir (Redwood): Perfect. We'll jump into the console, show per-route dashboards, then demo the cost breakdown and Optimize recommendations. Apologies in advance, screen share might blink a bit, network is meh today.
[00:33] Tom (Mira): No worries, we get that.

[02:05] Samir (Redwood): Ok, so here is the usage analytics page. Top-left you see total tokens, request rate, error rate. We're already filtering to production routes, you can toggle dev/prod, model version, and time window.
[02:28] Samir (Redwood): Notice the per-route card — you can expand a route to see model used, average latency p95, token count, and cost contribution. So this route is 18% of tokens but it's 42% of cost because it's using the 70B model and long context windows.
[03:15] Aisha (Mira): That is helpful. So the dashboard will show that a route is expensive even if usage is moderate. Can we see token-level cost and embeddings separately?
[03:28] Samir (Redwood): Yes — there's a cost breakdown tab. It splits by generation tokens, input tokens, and embeddings. For embeddings we also show per-embedding unit cost and the most expensive embedding routes.
[03:45] Priya (Mira): What about multi-model fallbacks? We sometimes want cheaper model for non-critical requests.
[03:55] Jordan (Redwood): Good question. Under routing you can set policies: prefer low-latency, prefer low-cost, or region-first. We also have canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks to a compatible quantized variant when higher tier is unavailable.

[06:20] Samir (Redwood): Now walk you through Optimize suggestions — here the system recommends batching sizes and suggests turning on KV prefix caching for routes with repeated prompts. It estimates the cost savings over the last 30 days and expected latency impact.
[06:45] Tom (Mira): How accurate are those savings estimates? We're sensitive — any overpromise bites us.
[06:54] Samir (Redwood): They're statistical; we analyze your traffic shape and give a conservative estimate range. For example, a route with high prefix reuse showed a projected 35-50% token cost reduction if KV caching were enabled, assuming similar traffic. We also provide the benchmark harness so you can validate on your own.

[09:10] Aisha (Mira): On healthcare data, PHI concerns are big. If we use hosted, is data stored? What's the retention?
[09:22] Jordan (Redwood): Hosted is opt-in on retention — default is minimal retention for debugging, and you can opt-out. For PHI we typically recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. We have KMS integrations and HSM support for private key storage, plus SOC2 controls. We'll send the SOC2 + network diagram after this call.
[09:41] Priya (Mira): We need audit logs for compliance and SSO.
[09:46] Samir (Redwood): Yes — audit logs are in Console -> Security, with per-token/ per-user traces tied to a request id. SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported.

[12:00] Samir (Redwood): Back to dashboards — here's the per-route latency distribution. You can drill into p50/p90/p95 and correlate with model version. This helps see if a slow tail is due to model size or infra.
[12:22] Tom (Mira): If we switch to dedicated GPUs, how do we predict throughput and cost?
[12:30] Jordan (Redwood): Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation. The console shows historical utilization and a capacity planner that maps QPS to GPU slots based on model profiles. For cost, we show committed monthly cost plus per-token delta if you burst into hosted.

[15:05] Aisha (Mira): There's often a tradeoff: low latency vs cost. Can we set SLOs per route?
[15:13] Samir (Redwood): Yep — routes can have SLOs and priority tiers. Routing will prefer nodes that meet the SLO; lower priority routes may be placed on cheaper hardware or queued to meet latency bounds.

[18:40] Samir (Redwood): Quick demo of a cost drilldown: pick a 7-day window, sort by cost contribution, then click into a route and you get a waterfall: model cost, infra cost, caching impact, and Optimize suggestions. See here — switching to a quantized 4-bit variant reduces compute cost 2.3x but adds small accuracy risk; we flag that.
[19:10] Priya (Mira): Can we run a dark launch where cheap model is tried and we measure quality?
[19:18] Jordan (Redwood): Yes — we support A/B as well as shadow/dark launches and automated regression testing against eval prompt sets. You can set automatic rollback if quality drops.

[22:00] Tom (Mira): About embeddings — we have vector search pipelines. If we move embeddings to dedicated, how do we measure unit economics?
[22:12] Samir (Redwood): Embeddings are tracked separately; console shows per-embedding unit cost, index storage, and typical query latencies. We have suggestions for batching and deduping embedding calls to reduce cost.

[25:30] Aisha (Mira): Any limitations on on-prem/air-gapped? We have strict PHI rules and might need an on-prem appliance.
[25:41] Jordan (Redwood): We have a Private on-prem package — control plane can be customer-hosted, and inference nodes live in your VPC. We support KMS and HSM integrations and can run an air-gapped deployment with agreed maintenance windows. There are extra support and licensing terms for that.

[28:50] Samir (Redwood): Now I'm running a quick profiler — you'll see how a route's average token latency changes when batching is increased. Note there is a sweet spot: too large batching increases latency for tail requests. The Optimize tab suggests per-route batch windows.
[29:20] Tom (Mira): Could you show the raw logs for a request id? We want to wire that into our internal tracing.
[29:29] Samir (Redwood): Sure — every request has an r_id that ties into tracing. You can export logs to your SIEM or pull via API.

[32:00] Priya (Mira): Regarding SLOs, if we need a 100ms p95 for a subset of routes, is that feasible?
[32:08] Samir (Redwood): It depends on model and sequence length. For short prompts on small-medium models, yes with dedicated low-latency instances. For long context or 70B models, 100ms is unrealistic. We can propose hybrid: route critical ones to smaller models or distilled variants.

[35:15] Aisha (Mira): Pricing: can you give an example mapping for our traffic? We're trying to compare cost if we stayed hosted vs reserved dedicated.
[35:27] Jordan (Redwood): We'll prepare a breakdown: current estimated monthly tokens * hosted per-token rates vs dedicated commit cost plus residual hosted burst. Expect dedicated to make sense if you have steady high throughput on big models. I'll send a model-specific TCO spreadsheet after the call.

[38:00] Samir (Redwood): One more note — Optimize also suggests kernel and quantization profiles. For instance, a model with 8-bit + KV cache enabled can hit similar latency at lower cost. But for compliance customers we sometimes prefer dedicated with standard FP16 to avoid any accuracy drift.

[40:45] Tom (Mira): Any references or case studies for healthcare customers?
[40:50] Jordan (Redwood): We have anonymized case studies and one-page references for regulated customers — I'll include those with the SOC2 docs.

[43:10] Priya (Mira): On the security checklist — SSO, audit logs, retention, and encryption at rest/in transit. Anything else?
[43:20] Samir (Redwood): Also IP & data residency controls, certificate pinning for private endpoints, and optional air-gapped deploys.

[46:00] Aisha (Mira): Ok, next steps?
[46:05] Jordan (Redwood): Recap: Jordan will send pricing + TCO spreadsheet, SOC2 + network diagram, and case studies. Samir will share the sample dashboard export and the benchmark harness. Mira will share traffic patterns and the SLOs they need. Then we schedule a technical deep dive to run the benchmark.
[46:28] Priya (Mira): Sounds good. Can we tentatively schedule the deep dive for next Friday?
[46:34] Jordan (Redwood): Tentative 2026-04-17 — we'll confirm after we get the traffic.

[49:00] Tom (Mira): One quick question — do you bill embeddings differently for distance search vs semantic ranking?
[49:08] Samir (Redwood): Embeddings are billed per-embedding unit; any downstream index/storage is separate if you use our vector DB add-on. For ranking we show per-request contribution in the console.

[50:55] Aisha (Mira): Great — appreciate the walk-through.
[51:02] Jordan (Redwood): Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and pricing.
[51:12] Priya (Mira): Bye all.
[51:15] Tom (Mira): Thanks.

End of recording.
